newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks track rising bonds to end higher.
newsitem.headline: French stocks track rising bonds to end higher.

text.p: French stocks finished higher on Monday, helped by firmer bond prices and good corporate results.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 15.55 points, or 0.78 percent, at 2,020.30, while the CAC-40 September futures contract closed six points higher at 2,022.50.
* Eurotunnel rallied 3.18 percent to close at 8.10 francs after reporting an operating breakeven for the first half of 1996.
* Cerus rallied on reports that it was in buyout negotiations with CGIP.
The reports suggested the deal was being engineered in such a way as to avoid a takeover bid for Valeo, in which Cerus holds 28 percent. Valeo shares fell 3.5 percent.

* Canal Plus rose after announcing plans late on Friday to merge with Nethold. It closed up 0.43 percent at 1,174 francs, off its highs, after outlining the impact of the deal on its results. It expects to break even in 1997, barring exceptionals, and EPS dilution until the year 2000.
* Casino fell 3.30 francs to 214 after its first-half operating results disappointed investors. Rival Carrefour benefitted, closing up 1.31 percent.

* Renault finished down 0.51 percent at 117.10 francs. The carmaker is due to report its first-half results on Tuesday afternoon and analysts' estimates range from a net attributable profit of 300 million francs to a net attributable loss of the same amount.
Rival PSA Peugeot Citroen finished up 1.05 percent at 575 francs.
